stories.primary_headline: Opposition's 'low-level acts' reinforce need for PM Modi's leadership: Kangana Ranaut

primary_source.headline: Opposition's 'low-level acts' reinforce need for PM Modi's leadership: Kangana Ranaut
primary_source.content: Raipur: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut on Sunday slammed opposition parties over their calls for regime change, stating that their "low-level acts" constantly remind the nation of the need for strong leadership under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Speaking to reporters at the Swami Vivekananda Airport here, the actor-politician cited recent unrest in France and global conflicts to emphasise that such developments make PM Modi's decisive leadership even more vital for India.Asked about the Opposition's remarks about regime change, she claimed, "Such low-level acts are repeatedly reminding the country that strong leadership is necessary. You saw what happened in France last night. Everything was set on fire, historical structures were destroyed, and looting took place."Delhi HC orders takedown of AI-generated obscene content on BJP MP Kangana RanautThe opposition parties have come under fire over senior advocate Prashant Bhushan’s "regime change" remark amid protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls.During a press conference earlier this week, Bhushan said spreading "disaffection" against a government is not a crime in a democracy, and that the struggle is now "really for a regime change". Several BJP leaders have reacted sharply to the remark.Ranaut said, "Everyone is watching the situation that has emerged around a possible Third World War. The Opposition is showing every day why India needs strong leadership in the form of Prime Minister Narendra Modi even more."The Mandi MP also condoled the death of 19 people in a stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, calling the incident extremely tragic while urging citizens to avoid visiting overcrowded venues during festivals.At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening after a surge in the crowd amid rains.

stories.primary_headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending

primary_source.headline: The problem with telling people the world is ending
primary_source.content: In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required. Continue reading...

stories.primary_headline: Move over, pervert glasses – the latest toxic trend is robogroping

primary_source.headline: Move over, pervert glasses – the latest toxic trend is robogroping
primary_source.content: Whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and womenYou may be familiar with rule 34 of the internet, which states that if something exists or can be imagined, there will almost certainly be online porn of it. Now let me introduce my rule 35: whenever a new technology is created, it will, without exception, immediately be used to harass girls and women.See, for example, Meta’s “pervert glasses”. As anyone could have foreseen, putting a tiny camera and microphone into smartglasses would immediately lead to people using them to record and harass women. Lo and behold, that is exactly what happened. So-called manfluencers have filmed themselves trying to flirt with women in public spaces and then uploaded the footage to TikTok. The women in these videos are often not aware they’ve been recorded until their identities are shared online and they are harassed by strangers. And what’s Meta doing about this? It’s instituted a few bans and made some privacy updates, but doesn’t seem to have an appetite to properly solve the problem. Indeed, at the Meta Connect 2026 keynote, Mark Zuckerberg did not feel the need to apologize to the women whose lives have been upended by his technology. Continue reading...
